1
Remix Move Guide
2
Almost every move in Remix has been changed to give it a useful purpose. Moves are buffed, retyped, renamed, and repurposed into fun new archetypes, expanding access to tools that fit many Pokemon. I have created MANY limited or exclusive distribution moves as well. The goal is meaningful choices between moves, with strong moves having workable drawbacks, and general synergies with items and abilities.
3
4
The overwhelming majority of moves have been changed or edited in some way, with less than a few dozen unchanged. It may feel overwhelming, but the changes are intuitive. Once you have an idea of how I approach things it should be relatively easy to know and understand what each move does and what category they fit into. It's all organized very thoroughly on this sheet to make it easier to understand.
5
I've rewritten ALL of the ingame move descriptions to reflect these changes as well, including percentages of effects, allowing you to see all of these edits in the real game without needing to check the sheet sometimes.
6
The DoozDex Extension is an invaluable tool you can have open on the sidebar while browsing Pokemon changes, allowing you to instantly search the movepools and effects of any Pokemon without needing to switch tabs.
The purpose of this move guide is to be used for understanding and viewing large groups and archetypes of moves, or if you can't use the extension- but the extension is a tool to quickly look up a move or refresh your memory on what a move does.
7
Everything is balanced around preparation and Nuzlocke battles against the trainer AI. Reliable attacks, healing, priority, and utility are more accessible, while powerful options have tradeoffs such as recoil, stat drops, limited PP, or restrictions on consecutive use. Items, abilities, and teammates can help overcome those drawbacks. Don’t depend on random effects to make your strategy work, but prepare for your opponent’s strongest possible outcome.

372
All Electric Type Moves
373
Paralysis has been buffed- now, moves will never miss a paralyzed opponent- AND it drops Speed by 75% again.
374
- Paralysis's main effect- being immobilized 25% of the time- is pretty useless for the player to abuse safely since it's inconsistent. Even with paraflinch, it's just not a reliable strategy, which is not what my hacks are designed around.
- Paralysis IS very dangerous when used against the player, since you have to prep as if you're being fully paralyzed every single turn.
375
- Paralysis's actual benefits for the player mostly come from lowering Speed. (In addition to doubling the power of Hex/Cheap Shot, Overload AND buffed Merciless)
- While this is useful, MANY other moves also lower speed now and allow the target to be statused on top of it.
376
- Now- Paralysis makes the opponent even more vulnerable to future attacks
- This does not work with inaccurate Sleep moves, of course- but it allows you to outspeed and kill a paralyzed Pokemon much easier.
- Pairs especially well with things like: High base power inaccurate moves or Hustle Pokemon + buffed Static, Nuzzle & more para-options.
- Thematically, I chose this because moving slower/being paralyzed making you an easier target to hit makes sense

Priority Attacking Moves
1018
Standard Priority Moves
In my games, priority moves are distributed much more and have fun synergies with various boosting abilities as well. While more Pokemon get them, and there are more priority moves (some types have both physical and special, some only fit or needed one, and Dragon didn't need any) they are still not 100% distributed to every single Pokemon if they don't make sense to use any. For example, I wouldn't give something like Wailord Aqua Jet, but it does make enough sense for Water Gun. These moves are useful in general to finish off weakened opponents before they can attack you, let alone if they are boosted by abilities or other multipliers. Infinite move relearner makes it easy to slot them on when needed.

First Impression Variants
There are only 2 "true" FIMP variants. Every other move is now reworked to gain priority on turn 1, but still work like a normal move on the following turns. This is not only convenient, but allows the AI to properly abuse these moves like regular attacks. They are ALL exclusive/limited distribution.

Stat Debuffing Attacking Moves
1104
Attacks That Drop Offensive Stats
All of these moves now drop both offensive stats for consistency and ease of remembering. They are very useful tools to make offensive progress and neutralize threats at once, but are limited compared to status moves. Status debuffing moves allow for a wider array or combination of stats to be dropped at once, have larger drops and are not capped in how often they can drop a stat. Their base power varies due to other factors like balancing around other moves of that type and category, or me wanting them to function better as useful coverage on top of debuffing utility.
1105
All of these moves have a caveat: The drop only triggers once per target.
Essentially, if you use Struggle Bug once on the opponent's first Pokemon, the first use will drop their stats, but the 2nd use won't. But if you swap to Disarming Voice after, you can drop them again to -2. And if you kill the first Pokemon, the "counter" resets for all of the moves, and you can drop their attacking stats again. This encourages using multiple moveslots or Pokemon, and other debuffing methods like status moves or abilities, instead of just relying on spamming one singular move to do it. It makes them less brainless but still very good attacks with defensive utility built-in.

1260
Stat Boosting Setup Moves
1261
This list excludes over a dozen attacking moves that boost the user's stats while dealing damage. To see those, click here.
1262
Setup moves are all heavily limited in either distribution, PP or priority.
- The low PP allows the AI to properly use them, and prevents the player from boosting excessively.
- The negative priority prevents the player from using Quick Claw to bypass Taunt leads or other anti-setup measures, and to just make it slightly harder.
Setup is one of the most broken things in an ingame nuzlocke context, even with all of the anti-setup measures I've put into place and how I construct my boss fights, it is still something that can be easy to snowball. Most powerful setup moves are learnt later in the game, or have very low distribution as well.

1320
Draco Meteor Variants
1321
One of my personal favorite move variants to use- they are very consistent, with a drawback that can be either situationally ignored or easily played around. These moves are essentially never going to work for the trainer AI, since they will not properly switch out after lowering their own stats. The player, however, enjoys using these- not even factoring in things like White Herb, Eject Pack, mixed attackers, crit moves ignoring your stat drops and more. These moves are on the radar to receive a PP decrease, but I am leaving them at 5 for now. They also deservedly decreased in power over time from OG Sweltering Sun to Scrambled to Remix. Regardless, these are some of the most powerful moves in the game.
The Normal and Dragon variants get to be stronger since they are essentially not super-effective on anything. Normal and Dragon moves in my games are stronger on average.

1358
Inaccurate Damaging Moves
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1359
You are NOT intended to use these moves without using any of the safety measures put in place to allow them to hit reliably.

My games are designed around nuzlockes and prepping, so these moves reward specific tool use such as abilities, items and more.
There are very few inaccurate moves in my games by design. The few that do exist are explicitly designed around several accuracy boosting methods:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1360
- Wide Lens is buffed to 50%, so these moves will never miss. There are also accuracy boosting abilities like Sixth Sense, Luminescent, Royal Decree & No Guard.
- Paralysis is buffed so that moves do not miss a paralyzed target, in addition to things like Static and buffed paralysis inflicting moves.
- Many moves (Damaging, setup and many Z-Moves too) now also boost Accuracy, allowing you to combo with these moves. A few moves also drop evasion.
- Gravity is buffed with Lunar Aura, and Telekinesis lasts indefinitely as well- both of which enable accuracy.

Recoil Moves
1398
These moves have very fair, reasonable drawbacks that you can play around, but they do stop mindless spamming of high base power moves.
- The 105 BP tier are mostly widespread moves which many Pokemon get access to via TM. They fit many Pokemon and are great coverage, which is why they are weaker.
- Several Pokemon have the abilities Reckless and Headstrong/Magic Guard, which negate recoil damage or boost the power of these moves.
- As usual, Normal & Dragon variants are higher BP or have stronger secondary effects.
- Shell Bell is buffed significantly to heal 1/4 of damage dealt. This heals off all recoil from the 105 BP tier, and almost entirely heals the recoil from the stronger ones.

These moves are very powerful and do not deal recoil or have other drawbacks- instead, they cannot be used 2x in a row.
They mostly function as Wicked Blow/Surging Strikes variants (despite those 2 moves not being present in Remix, since they are not needed), and are weaker than other 120+ BP moves, but the drawback is easier to work around. The main downside being that you cannot spam them especially with Choice Items, while you can "spam" recoil or other moves easier.

50% Crit Rate Moves
These +2 crit moves are designed so that they player has to use their item slot for Scope Lens to reliably get the power boost.
- There are other crit boosting methods such as the ability Super Luck or moves that boost crit rate via Z-Effects.
- However, when playing against the trainer AI- you should prepare as if they are getting the crit/play around both scenarios.
- This is the same safe prep/nuzlocking logic I balance inaccurate moves and non-guaranteed secondary effects around.
- The player should not bank on non-guaranteed secondary effects nor landing crits on any of these 50% crit moves.

1499
Multi-Hit Moves
1500
Moves that hit multiple times are very useful for the player to bypass common barriers like Focus Sashes, Sturdy, Multiscale/Energy Shield, type-weakening berries and more. They also get amazing synergy with strong abilities like Technician, Skill Link and Rapid Fire.
1501
2-5 Hit Moves/Variable Hit Moves
As usual with RNG in my games, these moves require the use of Loaded Dice for 4 hits, or Skill Link for 5 hits- otherwise, you should play as if you are getting minimum rolls. However, the AI can abuse these moves and you must play if they hit between min or max hits- while still being able to hold an actual item alongside them.
They are much stronger than the other multi-hit moves on average, with the drawback being the limitation of the item slot or your ability being Skill Link.

1682
Generic Drawback Free Attacks
1683
This list excludes all signature or exclusive moves, and any moves with a drawback or a unique effect that is listed in the other categories.
Essentially, this is a list of every generic attacking move that doesn't fit into other categories AND that doesn't have a drawback.
The most common drawbacks include no 2x in a row, inaccuracy, dropping your attacking stats, or dealing recoil damage and other examples.
Secondary effects/other categories include boosting your stats, dropping the foe's offensive stats or speed, draining moves, pivoting and more.
These moves are all 100 BP or less for the most part. Any move with over 95-100 BP has a drawback or very limited distribution.

1793
Sleep Moves
1794
Sleep has been reworked in my games to be much more reliable. Sleep will ALWAYS last for 2 turns unless specified otherwise.
This now also includes sleep induced from drowsiness like Yawn or abilities like Soporific. Drowsiness is especially good since the AI will not switch out to avoid falling asleep, unlike a real player. To compensate, most sleep moves require the use of Wide Lens or other accuracy boosting methods. The ones that are 100% accurate have limited distribution. They also all have limited PP to prevent constant cycling of putting the AI to sleep.
1795
The consistent sleep turns make it much safer to play around using these moves. If you are faster, you "skip" the foe's turn by putting them to sleep. That counts as 1 turn. Then you get a completely free turn guaranteed, and then they will wake up on the next turn. Since you are faster, you can knock them out before they wake up.
1796
If you are slower, you get TWO full turns of sleep in exchange for not instantly putting them to sleep before they can move on the first turn. This is huge since you can switch out and abuse a free guaranteed turn on an ally as well. With fast sleep, you can't do that unless the Pokemon you switch into is also faster and can knock them out before they wake up. Both fast and slow sleep enable setup, but slow sleep is even better for setting up.

1812
Reliable Paralyzing Moves
1813
Paralysis has been buffed- now, moves will never miss a paralyzed opponent- AND it drops Speed by 75% again.
1814
- Paralysis's main effect- being immobilized 25% of the time- is pretty useless for the player to abuse safely since it's inconsistent. Even with paraflinch, it's just not a reliable strategy, which is not what my hacks are designed around.
- Paralysis IS very dangerous when used against the player, since you have to prep as if you're being fully paralyzed every single turn.
1815
- Paralysis's actual benefits for the player mostly come from lowering Speed. (In addition to doubling the power of Hex/Cheap Shot, Overload AND buffed Merciless)
- While this is useful, MANY other moves also lower speed now and allow the target to be statused on top of it.
1816
- Now- Paralysis makes the opponent even more vulnerable to future attacks
- This does not work with inaccurate Sleep moves, of course- but it allows you to outspeed and kill a paralyzed Pokemon much easier.
- Pairs especially well with things like: High base power inaccurate moves or Hustle Pokemon + buffed Static, Nuzzle & more para-options.
- Thematically, I chose this because moving slower/being paralyzed making you an easier target to hit makes sense

Reliable Burning Moves
Now ALL thaw the user!
1832
Burn is one of the most reliable debuffing methods available, since crits do not bypass the drop unlike regular Attack drops. Because of this, Will-O-Wisp only has 2 PP since it has wide distribution to most Fire & Ghost types and other Pokemon too. Burning Bulwark has limited distribution.
Many of the strong, high BP burning moves are less useful for debuffing since they're so strong you're usually trying to kill things with them- but it's still a very useful side effect that requires an accuracy boost to use reliably. 1932
Soak Variants
1933
These moves are very unique, and some of my personal favorites to use. The primary benefit of using these is that they remove the STAB of the opponent, making them weaker without crits bypassing the drop compared to a typical stat drop. Another huge benefit outside of that is that you can synergize with teammates, super-effective moves, or even some specific Pokemon with a STAB type that is super-effective on the move they can use. (For example, a Rock/Fire type with Kindle, or a Water/Electric with Soak, and many other examples.) You can also use these with HP draining STAB moves for even more synergy. Lastly, the Z-Effects granting free offensive boosts is quite useful to 1v1 things easier. Many of the signature/exclusive variants of these also deal damage or have useful effects that compile on top of the type-change effect.

1946
Protect Variants
1947
Protect is too easily exploited with infinite move relearning- enabling free stall vs the AI which can't play around it.
It also trivializes Quick Claw on the AI, since you can just Protect to waste it. It also trivializes restrictions like guaranteed-crit moves being unusable twice in a row. There are several Pokemon that get no 2x in a row moves alongside one of these Protect variants- I just don't want it to be EVERY Pokemon. It also acts as a nerf to Speed boost, and requires the player to rely on the riskier Endure to stall turns in some situations. Many Pokemon all together can learn these Protect variants, and several slow, defensive Pokemon or fitting Pokemon keep Protect itself earlygame. I just didn't want every single Pokemon to be able to mindlessly slap on the TM for Protect to cheese or counter many things the AI can't play around, especially to get free turns for Black Sludge/etc, Leech, Ingrain, Poison and other passive damage on any Pokemon.
1948
The PP and distribution of many Protect variants is limited since their effects are so powerful, statusing, debuffing or damaging the opponent just for attacking.
